A browser has no filesystem, so every template and partial is handed to the engine up front.Teddy is listed twice, and it is the only engine here that is. Every other engine in this table renders one way: it turns a template into a JavaScript function and calls it. Teddy can do that, and it can also render by walking the node tree its compiler built, without writing any JavaScript at all. Those are two different renderers, not two ways of arriving at the same one, which is why the route changes the number for Teddy and for nobody else. Both rows are real ways to run it, and which one an app gets depends on whether it has a build step:Teddy (emitted js) is the emitted JavaScript, written out by teddy.precompile() in Node and loaded as a script. Faster, and it needs a build step and a known set of templates.Teddy (tree walk) is what a page gets with no build step at all: drop in the browser build and render. It is also the only thing that can render a template that does not exist until runtime, which is what a live editor or a template fetched from a server needs.Ratios are against Teddy (emitted js), since that is the like for like against the other engines here, all of which are running a compiled function too.Variables28 interpolations, one of them escaped html and one of them raw html. title: Teddy — Changelog (2.3.3)
text: 2.3.3Shrank production bundleUpdated dependencies.2.3.2Fixed a variable whose name is built from another variable, such as {names.{key}}, writing its value unescaped when the page went through a layout. A name not in the model was written back with flags the model supplied, and the layout parsed it again.Fixed a {variable} inside an escaped value being written unescaped when its |s flag was spelled oddly, such as {x||ss}, or when its name was built from another variable.Updated dependencies.2.3.1Breaking: Bumped the precompiled format to 4, so templates precompiled with an earlier version must be precompiled again.Fixed a variable whose name is built from another variable, such as {names.{key}}, taking its flags from the value it was built from. A model value ending in |s or |p|s made the variable write its value unescaped. Its flags now come only from the template, such as the |s in {names.{key}|s}.Updated dependencies.2.3.0Breaking: Bumped the precompiled format to 3, so templates precompiled with an earlier version must be precompiled again.Breaking: Changed and conditions whose value contains a {variable} to now compare against what the variable resolves to, as and always have. They used to compare against the value as written, so a template relying on that will render differently.Added support for {variables} in every attribute of a Teddy element: key and val, css and js, as, mode, and hydrate, and the names of elements, as through and src already did. An as, mode, or hydrate holding a variable is checked once a render has resolved it, with the same rules and errors as one written out.Added support for {variables} and ${variables} in a condition's name, such as or a one-line if-names.{person}="girl".Altered conditions to compare a value written with |p or |s, such as , against the variable's value. |p used to make it compare against the placeholder the value is held out as.Fixed and {variable} looking up the variable with the flag still attached to its name, so a variable that was present in the model was treated as missing and rendered as empty under |h or as {variable} under |d.Fixed a ${variable} whose name is built from another variable, such as ${names.{key}}, dropping its $ when it didn't resolve. A plain ${variable} already kept it.Fixed the client-side build splitting an attribute name at a {, }, or $, which broke one-line ifs and names holding a variable.Updated dependencies.2.2.0Added teddy.renderFragment(template, model, options), which renders into a DocumentFragment rather than a string. An element written with a ref attribute is handed back by name in the fragment's refs.Added teddy.check(template), which compiles a template without rendering it and returns its warnings, so a build step can fail on them.Added render options: teddy.render(template, model, options) takes verbosity, emptyVarBehavior, and cache for that render alone. A callback can still be passed third, as Express does, or fourth after options.Added npm run benchmark:compare, which measures how fast teddy is at two versions, by default this checkout against main, and says which scenarios got faster or slower, by how much, and whether that's more than the measurements disagree with themselves. See benchmarker/BENCHMARKER.md.Improved client-side rendering performance. Precompiled templates now render about 1.5× as fast, and cached templates up to a quarter faster.Altered warnings to now name the template they're about. Warnings that only printed at a higher verbosity are worded to say what was removed.Altered npm run benchmark to rebuild teddy if its build is older than its source, rather than only if it's missing, so a run never measures a build left over from another branch.Fixed {varName|p} writing its value unescaped. |p is meant only to stop the value being parsed, so it's now escaped like any other variable. Combine it with |s ({varName|s|p}) to write a value unescaped and unparsed.Fixed teddy.render adding a _noTeddyBlocks property to the model it was given, which threw on a frozen model. A render now keeps what it holds out of the markup to itself.Fixed an element in an included template keeping only the first of its one-line ifs: an element can carry several, but in a template brought in by , the ones after the first were dropped.Fixed selected-value and checked-value never matching a value written with the |p flag, on either side, such as
